means.en: The money earned in trade or business after paying the costs of producing and selling goods and services.
What a business has when it spends more than it collects.

plain.en: turning an idea into a business

means.en: The process through which a person, or a group of people, turns an idea into a business.

plain.en: a person who starts a business

means.en: A person who turns an idea into a business: spots a problem, takes risks, makes the key decisions, brings together the factors of production and adds to the welfare of society.

plain.en: a new idea put to use

means.en: A new product, recipe or way of working, such as nimbu pani with mint.
A collection of old Indian stories. One tells how a poor young man built a fortune starting from a dead mouse.

plain.en: an old building of small homes

means.en: An old building of many floors, with small one-room homes.

plain.en: a business owned equally by its members

means.en: A business in which every member is an equal owner and profits are shared equally, as at Lijjat Papad.
The total money a business gets from its sales.

plain.en: earning and deciding about your own money

means.en: Able to earn your own money and decide how to use it.

plain.en: a loan to buy a house or land

means.en: A special type of loan used to buy a house or land, with something valuable kept as security.

plain.en: a written plan for a business

means.en: A written document that explains the goals of a business and the steps to reach them.
The first amount of money a business needs to start, for equipment, rent, salaries, ingredients and packaging.
Recording, organising and reporting the money a business takes in and pays out, so the owner knows how it is doing.
Telling people about a business, for example on social media, on posters, with special offers or in advertisements.

plain.en: goods and materials a business holds

means.en: The goods, materials and other things a business holds to make products or to sell them.

plain.en: the four main areas of a business

means.en: Management and operations, finance and accounting, human resources, and marketing and sales.
Planning, organising and guiding the use of resources to reach the goals of the business.
Producing goods or services and delivering them well and on time.
Planning, getting and using money so the business can run and grow.
The total money a business earns from selling its goods and services.
The money a business spends on running, such as rent, salaries and raw materials.
The money coming into a business and going out of it.

plain.en: a record of profit or loss

means.en: A record that shows whether a business made a profit or a loss over a time, such as a month or a year.
The people an entrepreneur employs, who add to the business.
The work of bringing in customers and persuading them to buy.
Total revenue minus total expenses, before tax is paid.
The profit left after tax is paid to the government.
Costs that do not change with how much a business makes, such as rent and equipment. Also called overhead costs.
Costs that rise when a business makes more, such as raw materials and packaging.

plain.en: putting money in for the future

means.en: Putting money or other resources into something, such as a machine or a business, in the hope that it brings income, profit or a rise in value later.
Extra money paid for the use of a loan.
The Nattukottai Chettiars of Tamil Nadu, a well-known traditional business community of traders, bankers and moneylenders.
Honest and fair ways of doing business.
Lending money to people the lender trusts, who trust the lender in return.
A young, early-stage company started by entrepreneurs to offer a new product or service.
Going on working hard even when things are difficult.

plain.en: startups and the help around them

means.en: A country's startups and everything around them that helps them grow.
A startup valued at over 1 billion dollars.
A government scheme that supports entrepreneurship and new startups.
A national policy framework launched by the government in 2020 to make India self-reliant through innovation and local solutions.
The government's vision to make India a fully developed nation by 2047, 100 years after independence.
Work by companies that supports society, such as education, the environment and healthcare.

plain.en: what a business needs to make things

means.en: The things a business needs, such as land, materials, machines, money and workers.
The well-being of people. An entrepreneur adds to the welfare of society.
Something valuable kept as security until a loan is paid back.

plain.en: another name for the profit and loss account

means.en: Another name for the profit and loss account, which shows whether a business made a profit or a loss over a period of time.

plain.en: meeting today's needs without harming the future

means.en: Meeting today's needs without harming the future.
